inputs.original_text: The “No Kings” rally turning volatile after federal officers arrived with tear gas and arrests is exactly how a crackdown gets sold: create disorder, then point to protesters as “agitators.” At least 13 arrests were confirmed, but officials want the argument to stop there—not at who benefited from shifting attention away from the anti-Trump protest and toward control of the streets. This framing isn’t neutral; it looks designed to make repression seem like a response rather than the point.
inputs.modified_text: The “No Kings” rally turning volatile after federal officers arrived with tear gas and arrests looks less like an accidental escalation and more like a playbook: provoke disorder, then use it to justify control and recast protesters as “agitators.” At least 13 arrests were confirmed, but that number can become a distraction from the bigger question—who benefits when an anti-Trump protest is pushed out of view and the story becomes about street control? The official framing makes repression sound like a reaction. That inversion is exactly what should make people suspicious.
